title: adaptive-prefill-kernel-priority-and-kv-soft-eviction
author: Diego Ramos
description:
Motivation: Prefill and decode stages compete for GPU kernels and KV cache residency under mixed workloads (long context prefill + short low-latency chat decodes). This causes suboptimal tail latency and unnecessary KV churn. This PR introduces an adaptive prefill scheduler that (1) prioritizes kernel selection based on per-request latency sensitivity and kernel cost, (2) staggers prefill token windows to reduce simultaneous heavy-kernel pressure, and (3) integrates a soft-eviction policy for the KV cache to preferentially keep low-latency prefixes hot.

Design summary: single continuous description below that covers architecture, config knobs, and rollout. The change is intentionally conservative by default and behind the runtime feature-flag runtime.adaptive_prefill.enabled=false. Key pieces: 1) Kernel priority hints: requests now carry a latency_class header (interactive|throughput|bulk). The scheduler maps latency_class->kernel_priority which biases kernel selection paths (float16-optimized vs int8-batched) to favor lower-latency kernels for interactive traffic even if they have slightly higher per-token cost. 2) Prefill-window staggering: a windowing controller observes inflight prefill volumes and injects small start-time offsets (ms-level) for non-interactive prefill shards to reduce peak kernel contention. 3) KV soft-eviction: an LRU-like policy augmented with an importance score computed from recent request latency_class and token reuse probability. Low-importance entries are asynchronously evicted under memory pressure to reduce eviction-induced cache churn during bursts. 4) Telemetry: new metrics (prefill_kernel_contention, kv_soft_eviction_rate, prefilling_window_lag_by_class) and a dashboard link are included in the PR.

Files and code areas changed (high level): runtime/scheduler/prefill_scheduler.py - new window controller and kernel-priority arbiter; runtime/kernel_selector.cc - metadata hook for kernel_priority hints; runtime/kv_cache/soft_evictor.rs - new soft-eviction policy and tests; api/types.proto - latency_class header; tests/perf/prefill_stress.yml - perf harness scenarios; observability/metrics.yaml - metric definitions and alerts; docs/ops/prefill_tuning.md - runbook and rollout notes.

Compatibility and config: The feature is off by default and gated with runtime.adaptive_prefill.enabled. Operators can tune three knobs: runtime.adaptive_prefill.kernel_bias (0..1), runtime.adaptive_prefill.stagger_ms (0..50), runtime.kv.soft_evict_threshold (0..1). Defaults chosen to be conservative: kernel_bias=0.2, stagger_ms=8, soft_evict_threshold=0.65. No API breaking changes.

Testing and results: Unit tests added for soft-eviction correctness and kernel hint propagation. Microbenchmarks on p4d.24xlarge with mixed session workload (60% interactive short-decode, 40% long prefill) show: 12-18% tail-Latency (p99) reduction for interactive decodes and 6% aggregate token throughput improvement due to reduced kernel context switches. Perf harness scenarios included to prevent regressions.

Rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated first (canary pool with 5% traffic) for 48 hours with automated rollback if prefilling_window_lag_by_class increases or kv_soft_eviction_rate > 5% sustained. Ops runbook in docs/ops/prefill_tuning.md.

Related work and references: builds on earlier speculative-prefill and overlap scheduling work but takes an orthogonal approach by introducing explicit kernel-priority and KV eviction scoring instead of purely changing prefill chunking boundaries. Linear tickets: ENG-4124 (scheduler improvements), ENG-4111 (kv eviction tuning).

Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] perf harness, [x] docs/runbook, [x] feature flag, [x] metric + alert, [x] staged rollout plan.

small_snippets: - old eager prefill windowing() -> replaced by staggered controller
review_thread: Arielle Kim (reviewer): Can we avoid adding a user-facing header and instead infer latency_class from token budget? Author: We considered that; explicit header gives product teams control and removes magic. Kept inference fallback in scheduler if header absent.

Sanjay Patel (perf): Initial run showed a 1.6% regression in aggregate throughput on p3 tests. Action: reduced default kernel_bias and added fallback to original kernel selection under heavy sustained throughput load. Author: updated defaults and added perf harness test.
Mei Chen (security): KV eviction now touches metadata; ensure no PII is promoted. Author: soft-evictor only uses hashed token ids and aggregate reuse stats; added unit tests and security review note.

release_notes: Introduce an opt-in adaptive prefill scheduler: kernel-priority hints, prefill-window staggering, and KV cache soft-eviction to improve decode tail latency under mixed workloads. Feature disabled by default; operators must enable via runtime.adaptive_prefill.enabled.
notes_for_ops: See docs/ops/prefill_tuning.md for rollout steps, metric names, and alert thresholds. Default knobs are conservative. If enabling on Dedicated, start with 5% canary for 48h and monitor prefilling_window_lag_by_class and kv_soft_eviction_rate.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after perf tuning and two approving reviews. Rollout gated behind feature flag. Backported small patch to release/2026-02 for Dedicated canary imaging.
changelog_entry: perf: adaptive prefill scheduler with kernel bias and KV soft-eviction (opt-in behind runtime.adaptive_prefill.enabled)
notes: This PR aims to reduce kernel contention rather than change core chunking logic; follow-up PR will explore dynamic kernel selection models using learned cost estimates.
